extracted.intended_audience: news editors, media reporters, accountability journalists, and readers of media criticism
extracted.subtask_description: A practitioner-oriented rubric that lists criteria Erik Wemple uses to judge when journalism (and newsroom behavior) is itself newsworthy, with tests for individual media stories and for whether outlets merit front-page treatment. Useful for deciding what media-related matters deserve accountability reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Falsehood-correction speed
rubrics_metrics.description: How fast did a network admit an error?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates timeliness of admitting mistakes; faster, prominent corrections are more newsworthy as evidence of accountability, while slow or obscured corrections indicate problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure adequacy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether relevant conflicts of interest or relationships were meaningfully disclosed to audiences; inadequate disclosure is a journalistic failing worth reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern-not-incident
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for systemic, repeating issues rather than isolated mistakes; patterns suggest institutional flaws and therefore higher newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-air vs. off-air discrepancies
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrepancies between public/on-air statements and private/off-air communications (e.g., leaked private comms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts between what journalists/hosts say publicly and what they say privately can reveal hypocrisy or hidden practices; such revelations elevate the story's significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel decisions revealing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel decisions (hires, firings, departures) that reveal newsroom standards and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use staffing moves as a lens on institutional norms—who is rewarded or punished, and what that signals about editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamation-suit risk surfaced
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether defamation litigation risk has been surfaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that expose legal exposure (or outcomes) for outlets or journalists are important indicators of accountability and potential consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction prominence and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: "Did you correct prominently or in a tweet at midnight?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not just whether a correction occurred but how prominently and when; burying a correction in a late tweet suggests insufficient accountability and lowers editorial credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchors held to same standard as reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: "Are anchors held to same standard as reporters?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether high-profile personalities are subject to the outlet's stated standards; differential treatment indicates hypocrisy or weak enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has outlet changed practice based on past errors
rubrics_metrics.description: "Has your outlet changed practice based on past errors?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses institutional learning—whether past mistakes prompted policy or practice changes; evidence of reform increases newsworthiness and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cable-news fact-pattern accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that documents fact-patterns in cable news revealing accountability issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevates stories that compile and analyze recurring fact patterns on cable news, showing systemic shortcomings rather than isolated slip-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamation litigation outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on the outcomes of defamation litigation involving media figures or outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal outcomes provide concrete measures of accountability and can substantively affect reputations and practices—worthy of attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departures of senior anchors/executives
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of departures of senior anchors or executives as revealing standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level departures often reflect institutional reckoning; reporting on them can illuminate enforcement of norms and consequences for misconduct or failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial-standards documents (newly issued)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication or revision of editorial-standards documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The issuance or change of formal standards is newsworthy because it codifies expectations and signals institutional priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on the reporting (revealing craft norms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-reporting that reveals craft norms and practices of the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories about how journalism is practiced—especially when they reveal norms, shortcuts, or ethical choices—are valuable accountability journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider gossip without policy implication (demoted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Insider gossip that lacks policy or standards implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such stories are demoted by the rubric: celebrity-style gossip about insiders is less newsworthy unless it ties to institutional standards or consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personality drama without standards angle (demoted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personality drama that lacks a standards or accountability angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalities' private conflicts or melodrama are not elevated unless they illuminate newsroom norms, policy failures, or credibility issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-credibility consequence test (overarching principle)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wemple's overarching orientation: accountability journalism should treat journalism itself as subject to scrutiny. A story's newsworthiness depends on whether it has meaningful consequences for the credibility, standards, or practices of the press.
